title: What Makes Evidence Strong
summary: Learn how relevance, completeness, provenance, specificity, and reviewability can make a work product more useful as evidence.
objectives: Identify characteristics that make an evidence candidate stronger or weaker.
Explain why provenance and relevance matter.
Recognize when an evidence candidate is incomplete or unclear.

vocab.def: How directly a piece of evidence relates to the skill, task, requirement, or question being considered.
Whether enough of the work and supporting context are present for meaningful review.
Whether a reviewer has enough clear information to examine the work against defined expectations.
Information about the task, project, conditions, and origin connected to the evidence.

sections.heading: Strong evidence is connected to a clear claim
sections.body: A work sample is most useful when it relates directly to the skill, responsibility, or competency being considered. More material is not automatically better if it does not answer the question.

sections.heading: Context helps the reviewer understand the work
sections.body: Useful evidence can identify the task, conditions, learner contribution, source, version, and expected result.

sections.heading: Completeness matters
sections.body: A partial screenshot, missing file, unclear recording, or unexplained result may make review difficult even when the learner did meaningful work.

sections.heading: Polish and proof are not the same
sections.body: A beautiful presentation can improve clarity, but appearance alone does not establish that a competency was demonstrated.

practice.prompt: Which is stronger evidence: a screenshot with no explanation or a work sample tied to a specific task, learner contribution, and source?
practice.answer: The work sample with clear task, contribution, and source context is stronger because it is easier to interpret and review.

practice.prompt: A polished slide deck contains no information about who completed the work or what task it came from. What is missing?
practice.answer: Important provenance and source context are missing.

quiz.question: What most strengthens an evidence candidate?
options: Clear relevance, provenance, completeness, and reviewable context
A learner declaring the work verified
quiz.answer: Clear relevance, provenance, completeness, and reviewable context

lab.objective: Compare several simulated evidence candidates and identify strengths, gaps, missing context, and improvements needed before review.

reflectionPrompt: What information would make one of your own projects easier for another person to review fairly?
